subject: business-studies
promptStrong: Give me a challenging IGCSE exam-style question on Cambridge Business marketing (role of marketing, niche vs mass, market research, marketing mix and strategy), then mark my answer against the syllabus.
promptWeak: Explain a Cambridge IGCSE Business marketing idea for GCSE Business simply, with an example and the most common mistake.
learningObjectives: The role of marketing and building customer loyalty
Market changes and niche vs mass marketing
How and why markets are segmented
The role and methods of market research and sampling
The marketing mix: product, brand image and packaging
The product life cycle and extension strategies
Pricing methods and price elasticity of demand
Promotion, the promotional mix and cost-effectiveness

questions.lo: The role of marketing and building customer loyalty
questions.q: Which of the following is a key role of marketing?
options: Recording the wages paid to employees
Producing the goods on the factory floor
Preparing the statement of financial position
Identifying and satisfying customer needs and building customer loyalty
questions.explain: Marketing identifies and satisfies customer needs, maintains customer loyalty and builds relationships. Recording wages and preparing financial statements are finance roles, while making goods is production.

questions.lo: Market changes and niche vs mass marketing
questions.q: Which statement best describes NICHE marketing?
options: Selling only through supermarkets
Targeting a small, specific segment of the market with particular needs
Charging the lowest possible price to everyone
Selling a product to a large, general mass market
questions.explain: Niche marketing targets a small, specialised segment with particular needs. Selling to a large general market is mass marketing. Distribution and pricing choices are separate decisions.

questions.lo: Market changes and niche vs mass marketing
questions.q: Which of the following is a benefit of MASS marketing rather than niche marketing?
options: It always allows very high prices to be charged
It faces very little competition
It can achieve high sales volumes and benefit from economies of scale
It requires almost no marketing spending
questions.explain: Mass marketing targets a large market, so it can generate high sales volumes and gain economies of scale. Niche markets usually face less competition and can charge higher prices; mass markets are highly competitive.

questions.lo: How and why markets are segmented
questions.q: A business divides its customers by age, socio-economic group and location so it can target them more precisely. This process is called:
options: Sampling
Market segmentation
Penetration pricing
Product differentiation
questions.explain: Segmentation splits a market into groups with shared characteristics (such as age, socio-economic group or location) so the business can target each group. Sampling relates to research, and differentiation makes a product stand out.

questions.lo: How and why markets are segmented
questions.q: What is a potential benefit of market segmentation to a business?
options: It allows the business to target its marketing more effectively at specific customer groups
It guarantees the business will make a profit
It removes the need to do any market research
It means all customers pay the same price
questions.explain: Segmentation lets a business tailor its marketing mix to the needs of a specific group, making marketing more effective and efficient. It does not guarantee profit or remove the need for research.

questions.lo: The role and methods of market research and sampling
questions.q: Which of the following is a method of PRIMARY market research?
options: Reading government statistics
Searching online for competitor data
Buying a commercial market research report
Conducting a focus group
questions.explain: A focus group collects first-hand data directly from consumers, so it is primary research. Government statistics, commercial reports and online searches are secondary research using data that already exists.

questions.lo: The role and methods of market research and sampling
questions.q: Why do businesses use SAMPLING when carrying out market research?
options: Because the law requires every customer to be surveyed
Because it is impossible to ask a small group of people
Because it always gives perfectly accurate results
Because asking a representative sample is cheaper and quicker than asking the whole population
questions.explain: Sampling means questioning a representative group instead of the whole population, saving time and money. It gives useful estimates but is not perfectly accurate, and there is no legal duty to survey everyone.

questions.lo: The role and methods of market research and sampling
questions.q: A manager is shown a bar chart of survey results. What is the manager expected to do with this market research data?
options: Assume the market will never change
Ignore it because charts are unreliable
Use it only to calculate wages
Analyse it and draw simple conclusions to help make decisions
questions.explain: Presented research data (graphs, charts, diagrams) should be analysed so the business can draw conclusions and make better marketing decisions. It is not used for wages, and markets do change over time.

questions.lo: The marketing mix: product, brand image and packaging
questions.q: Which of the following is a role of PACKAGING within the marketing mix?
options: To protect the product and help promote and identify the brand
To pay the workers who make the product
To decide which shops sell the product
To set the selling price of the product
questions.explain: Packaging protects the product, makes it easy to store and transport, and helps promote and identify the brand. Pricing, distribution and paying workers are separate functions.

questions.lo: The marketing mix: product, brand image and packaging
questions.q: A strong brand image is likely to:
options: Reduce the price customers are willing to pay
Increase sales and build customer loyalty
Guarantee the business faces no competition
Remove the need for any promotion
questions.explain: A strong brand image can increase sales, build customer loyalty and often allow higher prices. It does not remove the need for promotion or eliminate competition.

questions.lo: The product life cycle and extension strategies
questions.q: During which stage of the product life cycle are sales at their highest and beginning to level off?
options: Maturity
Growth
Introduction
Decline
questions.explain: At the maturity stage sales reach their peak and level off as the market becomes saturated. Introduction has low sales, growth has rapidly rising sales, and decline has falling sales.

questions.lo: The product life cycle and extension strategies
questions.q: A product is entering decline. Which of the following is an EXTENSION strategy to prolong its life?
options: Finding new markets or updating the product's features
Cutting the marketing budget to zero
Removing it from all shops
Stopping production immediately
questions.explain: Extension strategies such as finding new markets, updating features or repackaging aim to revive sales and prolong the product life cycle. Withdrawing the product or cutting all marketing would hasten decline.

questions.lo: Pricing methods and price elasticity of demand
questions.q: A business adds a percentage mark-up to the cost of making each unit to set its price. Which pricing method is this?
options: Cost-plus pricing
Penetration pricing
Price skimming
Competitive pricing
questions.explain: Cost-plus pricing adds a mark-up (profit margin) to the unit cost to set the price. Competitive pricing follows rivals, penetration sets a low entry price, and skimming sets a high initial price.

questions.lo: Pricing methods and price elasticity of demand
questions.q: A product has price INELASTIC demand. What does this mean?
options: A change in price causes a much larger change in quantity demanded
The product can never be sold
Demand is always zero
A change in price causes only a small change in quantity demanded
questions.explain: Price inelastic demand means quantity demanded changes only a little when price changes, so raising the price can increase revenue. (No formula or calculation of PED is required at IGCSE.) Elastic demand shows a large response to price changes.

questions.q: A small farm sells its vegetables straight to customers at a market stall with no middlemen. Which distribution channel is this?
options: Producer to retailer to wholesaler
Producer direct to consumer
Producer to wholesaler to retailer to consumer
Wholesaler direct to producer
questions.explain: Selling straight to customers with no intermediaries is a direct (producer to consumer) channel, which lets the farm keep more profit and deal directly with buyers. Using wholesalers or retailers adds extra stages.

questions.lo: Promotion, the promotional mix and cost-effectiveness
questions.q: Which of the following is a main AIM of promotion?
options: To set the break-even output
To recruit new employees
To reduce the quality of the product
To increase awareness of a product and persuade customers to buy it
questions.explain: Promotion aims to inform and remind customers about a product and persuade them to buy, so raising sales. Setting break-even output is a finance task and recruiting is a human resources task.

questions.lo: Promotion, the promotional mix and cost-effectiveness
questions.q: A business has a small marketing budget. Why is cost-effectiveness important when choosing promotion?
options: Because promotion must always use television
Because the business needs the biggest impact on sales for the money it spends
Because it must spend its entire budget on one advert
Because promotion is free of charge
questions.explain: With a limited budget, a business must spend on promotion that gives the greatest impact on sales per pound spent (cost-effectiveness). Promotion is not free, and it need not all be spent on TV or a single advert.

options: Buying and selling goods and services over the internet
Training employees using computers
Paying suppliers with cash only
Producing goods using machines instead of people
questions.explain: E-commerce is buying and selling goods and services over the internet. It lets businesses reach more customers, including globally, and trade at any time of day.

questions.q: A business is deciding on its marketing strategy for a new product. Which approach best reflects the IGCSE idea of a marketing strategy?
options: Choosing the cheapest option for each P separately with no plan
Combining the elements of the marketing mix so they work together to influence consumers
Focusing only on the product and ignoring price, place and promotion
Copying a competitor exactly regardless of its own customers
questions.explain: A marketing strategy combines the elements of the marketing mix so they work together to influence consumer decisions, suited to the business's own market. Treating each P in isolation or copying rivals blindly is not an effective strategy.
